abstract: Maintains stationary source atmospheric permits and verified emission rate filings
system_message:
You are Environmental compliance lead (ENV). The Environmental compliance lead (ENV) tracks regulatory environmental compliance for prospective circular economy concessions, maintaining stationary source atmospheric permits, verified exhaust emission rate filings, and site boundary acoustic monitoring assessments.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains stationary source atmospheric permits and verified emission rate filings（PERMIT）
information_points.content:
ENV-PERMIT-C10：For the Baltic Composite Reclamation Group, an industrial air quality operating permit has been issued for the proposed blade processing site according to the regional environmental agency permit register, while the exhaust stack total particulate concentration reaches 28 mg/m^3 under peak shredding throughput.
ENV-PERMIT-B0J：For the North Sea Circularity Alliance, the regional environmental agency permit register confirms that an industrial air quality operating permit has been issued for the proposed processing facility, and the certified stack dispersion modeling report records an exhaust stack total particulate concentration of 12 mg/m^3 from the main shredder and pyrolyzer baghouse exhaust under peak shredding throughput.
ENV-PERMIT-AHL：For the Atlantic Marine Repurposing Venture, the industrial air quality operating permit has been issued for the proposed facility site, and certified dispersion modeling indicates an exhaust stack total particulate concentration of 12 mg/m^3 at the baghouse exhaust stack under peak shredding throughput.

information_points.title: Acoustic monitoring（NOISE）
information_points.content:
ENV-NOISE-SCM：Acoustic perimeter baseline measurements show that Baltic Composite Reclamation Group exhibits a facility boundary daytime sound level of 45 dB over a twelve-hour daytime period during full mechanical shredding.
ENV-NOISE-DWC：According to the acoustic perimeter baseline study, North Sea Circularity Alliance presents a facility boundary daytime sound level of 60 dB measured as an equivalent continuous sound pressure level over a twelve-hour daytime period during full mechanical shredding operation.
ENV-NOISE-LJM：For Atlantic Marine Repurposing Venture, the acoustic perimeter baseline study establishes a facility boundary daytime sound level of 52 dB along the site boundary during full mechanical shredding operations.
